sources.credibility: official WisdomTree launch press release (issuer of PUTW), primary source for inception date and mechanism
sources.core_claim: WisdomTree launched PUTW on NYSE Arca on 2016-02-24 to track the CBOE S&P 500 PutWrite Index (PUT); the fund sells at-the-money, European-style, one-month SPX puts against a fully collateralized T-bill account, rolled monthly.
sources.project_applicability: Grounds PUTW_HOLD's proxy inception date (2016-02-24) and monthly rebalance frequency in candidate-manifest.json.
sources.reflection: Marketing release, not the prospectus; no live NAV performance is claimed here, only the mechanism and launch date, which are not the kind of fact that decays.

sources.credibility: Cboe's own official strategy-index fact sheet, primary exchange source
sources.core_claim: PUT index launched 2007-06-20 (first value 2007-01-03); annualized return 7.1%, volatility 10.7%, max drawdown -32.7%, Sharpe 0.52 (vs S&P 500 TR 11.0%/15.4%/-50.9%/0.61) from 2007-01-03 through 2026-08-31; SPX puts sold monthly, usually 3rd Friday, at-the-money.
sources.project_applicability: Independent confirmation of the mechanism PUTW tracks and a long-run index-level Sharpe used only as outside context, not as a substitute for our own K1/K2 test.
sources.reflection: Index-level, not net of PUTW's ~0.38% expense ratio or tracking error; would need our own backtest for a real, cost-adjusted number -- moot here since PUTW data is unobtainable through our vendor.

sources.credibility: Oleg Bondarenko, University of Illinois at Chicago; CBOE-commissioned academic study, SSRN working paper, updates a 2016 predecessor study
sources.core_claim: Over 32 years (1986-2018), PUT index annual compound return 9.54% vs S&P 500 9.80% (comparable) but PUT's annualized Sharpe 0.65 vs S&P 500's 0.49 (substantially better risk-adjusted); PUT's standard deviation 9.95% vs S&P 500's 14.93%; over 2006-2018 PUT's Sharpe was 0.50 vs S&P 500's 0.51 (roughly tied) with PUT max drawdown -32.7% vs S&P 500 -50.9%.
sources.project_applicability: Independent, peer-reviewable evidence on the PUT index mechanism PUTW tracks; used only as background -- this round never reaches a backtest of PUTW_HOLD itself because the underlying data is unobtainable.
sources.reflection: Index-level historical study using bid-quote-based historical option pricing for pre-2007 data (disclosed by the author), not audited trade data; recent-period (2006-2018) Sharpe roughly ties the S&P 500, a much weaker edge than the full 32-year number, consistent with the registry's general skepticism of cherry-picked long windows.

sources.credibility: Ennis Knupp + Associates, independent institutional investment consultant, commissioned study hosted on Cboe's own site
sources.core_claim: June 1986-October 1998: PUT index annualized return 10.32% (before fees), volatility 9.91%, Sharpe 0.63 vs S&P 500's 8.77%/15.39%/0.30; PUT underperforms in strongly rising months (48.7% of months) and outperforms in flat/declining months (51.3% of months).
sources.project_applicability: Independent third-party (not CBOE, not WisdomTree) confirmation of the same regime-dependent return profile; reinforces that PUTW_HOLD's expected value is state-dependent, relevant context if the data blocker is ever resolved.
sources.reflection: 2008 report, pre-financial-crisis final data point (Oct 2008), so it does not capture the 2008 crash's effect on the index; superseded in coverage by the more recent Bondarenko (2019) and Cboe (2026) fact sheet above.

sources.credibility: arXiv preprint, not yet peer-reviewed; quantitative finance methods paper on short-dated index-option put-writing
sources.core_claim: Studies Kelly-criterion, VIX-based and hybrid position sizing for very short-dated (0-5 DTE) SPXW put-writing; finds a hybrid sizing method balances return generation with drawdown control, especially in low-volatility regimes (2024), and that far out-of-the-money, ultra-short-dated options have better risk-adjusted returns than longer-dated/closer-to-money alternatives.
sources.project_applicability: Confirms active academic interest in put-writing sizing is recent (2025) and orthogonal to PUTW_HOLD (monthly, at-the-money, buy-and-hold) -- a genuinely different, more sophisticated mechanism than this round's simple proxy; not preregistered here since it requires 0-5 DTE options data we do not have.
sources.reflection: Not opened in full (abstract/summary only); flags a possible future direction (short-dated put-writing with position sizing) distinct from and more promising than the static PUTW proxy, worth a separate direction entry rather than folding into this blocked one.

sources.credibility: official Journal of Derivatives (Institutional Investor Journals / Portfolio Management Research) publisher page for the peer-reviewed article; full text is paywalled and was not opened in this pass -- existence, authorship, journal and issue confirmed via the publisher's own page plus corroborating listings (whaley.info author page, ResearchGate)
sources.core_claim: Robert Whaley (Vanderbilt University), commissioned by Cboe, published 'Return and Risk of CBOE Buy-Write Monthly Index' in The Journal of Derivatives, vol. 10 no. 2 (Winter 2002), pp. 35-42 -- the peer-reviewed methodology paper underlying the CBOE BuyWrite index family that the PutWrite index (PUT), and PUTW's tracked index, descend from.
sources.project_applicability: Establishes that the PUT index's collateralized-options-overlay design descends from a peer-reviewed academic methodology (Whaley 2002), not an ad hoc index-provider construction; background only.
sources.reflection: Abstract/existence-level citation only -- the paywalled full text was not opened, so no specific number from this paper is used in any gate; included for provenance, not as quantitative evidence.

sources.credibility: Cboe's own official methodology document for the PutWrite index family (PUT, WPUT)
sources.core_claim: Official Cboe Global Indices methodology document covering the S&P 500 PutWrite index family; cover page confirmed opened, full text not machine-extractable from the fetched PDF in this pass (binary/compressed stream), so no further quantitative claim is drawn from it here.
sources.project_applicability: Confirms Cboe maintains a distinct, versioned methodology document for this index family (beyond the marketing fact sheet already cited); not used for any specific number.
sources.reflection: Honest limitation: opened but not text-extractable this pass; the two other Cboe/WisdomTree documents above already supply the mechanism details actually used.
